title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: part of the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' following La Longue Marche. Grothendieck is studying algebraic group schemes attached to a pair of elements rho, sigma of GL2. In the 'cas modulaire' of the previous page, rho = [[0,1],[-1,1]] has order 6 and sigma = [[0,-1],[1,0]] has order 4; these generate SL2(Z). Notation used below: T_rho and T_sigma are the centralizers of rho and sigma, which are tori when rho and sigma are regular. N'_sigma is a normalizer-type extension of T_sigma, and delta_sigma = det : N'_sigma -> G_m. B'_0 is a Borel-type subgroup of G with unipotent part Lambda_0, which is isomorphic to G_a via lambda -> epsilon_0(lambda), presumably the matrix [[1,lambda],[0,1]].

The previous page dévisses SG^*_{rho,sigma}(0) into a connected part (a torus extended by G_m, cut out by det a = det b) and a mu_2 x mu_2 quotient, using a semidirect product decomposition (22). To finish describing the structure, one needs the conjugation action of SG^*_{rho,sigma}(0) on Lambda_0. On this page, SG^*_{rho,sigma}(0) is viewed as a subgroup of T_rho x N'_sigma and Lambda_0 as G_a.

The key relation is u epsilon_0(lambda) u^{-1} = epsilon_0(det(u) lambda), with det(u) = det(b) = delta_sigma(b). This is the standard fact that a torus acts on the root group through a character, here the determinant. Hence the action factors through the character (27): SG^*_{rho,sigma}(0) -> N'_sigma -> G_m (via delta_sigma). Grothendieck marks this 'OK'.

He then introduces a homomorphism (28), t: G^*_{rho,sigma} -> G. Using the scheme decomposition G^*_{rho,sigma} = B'_0 x T_rho x N'_sigma, t is identified with the first projection (u,a,b) -> u, viewed in G via the inclusion B'_0 into G. He also announces a parametrization u = Theta(alpha, beta, mu, epsilon). The next page characterizes Theta, up to a mu_2-valued sign ambiguity, by formulas giving u(rho), u(sigma) and det u.

The purpose is to describe explicitly the group scheme of 'symmetries' of the pair (rho, sigma), presumably for the loop-equation / Teichmüller-tower analysis.
errors: Machine transcription renders the projection as (u,a,b) -> a; since it is viewed in G via B'_0 into G, it must be (u,a,b) -> u. No mathematical error is evident; the computation u epsilon_0(lambda) u^{-1} = epsilon_0(det(u) lambda) is consistent with a torus acting on a root group through the determinant character, given an appropriate normalization of the embedding.

ideas.what: Action of a torus or normalizer on a unipotent root subgroup via the determinant character, so the action factors through delta_sigma: N'_sigma -> G_m
ideas.modern_name: torus action on root groups via roots/characters; semidirect product structure of a Borel subgroup
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard theory of algebraic groups (Chevalley, Borel; SGA3)
ideas.where_published: SGA 3 (general theory of tori and root data)

ideas.what: Defining a homomorphism G^*_{rho,sigma} -> G as the projection to the B'_0 factor of a scheme-theoretic product decomposition
ideas.modern_name: explicit parametrization of a stabilizer group scheme of a pair of elements of GL2
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure (no standard reference for this specific construction)

deep.surprise_reason: Routine bookkeeping computation within a longer unpublished construction: an action of a torus on G_a through a character, plus the definition of a projection map. Nothing new beyond the context of the larger project.
transcription_corrections: '(u, a, b) -> a' should read '(u, a, b) -> u' (the B'_0 component).

In (27), 'SG^*_{rho,sigma}(0)' carries the same superscript (*0 / d-phi-like mark) as in the first lines; the scribble is uncertain.
